Fit, per site, the effect of a per-run trait on logit occupancy, with mzLib's SiteTraitEffects

ptmqtl_trait_effects.Rd

Per site, the effect of a per-run trait on logit occupancy, from a random-intercept mixed model per site, so that repeated runs of one biological replicate are not counted as independent.

The model, per site, is logit(occupancy) = b0 + b_trait x trait + covariates + a random intercept per biological replicate + error, fitted by REML (mzLib's MixedModel). The random intercept is the point: repeated runs of one animal or donor are not counted as independent, so a trait that is constant within each replicate is tested at the between-replicate degrees of freedom.

Usage

ptmqtl_trait_effects(occupancy, runs, min_runs = NULL, min_replicates = NULL,
  logit_epsilon = NULL, keep_ceiling = FALSE, timeout = 600)

Arguments

occupancy

The table ptmqtl_occupancy writes with out (columns found by header name). A fraction cell is used as written, as mzLib does for a stored fraction.

runs

A TSV with a header row, then one row per run: the run, its biological replicate, the trait (its header names it; any unit), then any covariates (each header names one). A run with a blank trait is not used.

min_runs

Fewest runs with a response for a site to be fitted (runs). NULL: mzLib's default (6 at mzLib d10017ce), which min_runs in the result reports.

min_replicates

Fewest distinct replicates among them (replicates). NULL: mzLib's default (4 at mzLib d10017ce).

logit_epsilon

Fractions are clamped to [epsilon, 1 - epsilon] before the logit (fraction, above 0 and below 0.5). NULL: mzLib's default (5e-5 at mzLib d10017ce).

keep_ceiling

Use runs where the site was seen only modified. FALSE sends nothing, so mzLib's default (leave them out) applies.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

Only quantified cells are responses. Floors, count-only and undetected cells are left out, never entered as 0, so this answers "does the modified share change?", not "is the modification detected more often?". Ceilings are left out by default.

Value

An mzlibr_trait_effects:

- records, a data.frame with one row per site with a usable response, by site key: site_key, protein_accession, position, residue and modification, as ptmqtl_occupancy writes them; status, one of "fitted", "below_support", "too_few_observations", "rank_deficient", "too_few_groups", "variance_ratio_at_limit" or "not_converged"; effect (logit occupancy per trait unit), the change in logit(occupancy) per unit of the trait, so exp(effect) is the odds ratio, NA when not fitted; standard_error (logit occupancy per trait unit); df (degrees of freedom), by the containment rule; p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), two-sided, for the trait; q, a fraction (0 to 1), Benjamini-Hochberg over this call's fitted sites; runs, runs contributing a response; replicates, distinct replicates among them; median_fraction (fraction, 0 to 1), median occupancy over those runs; covariate_effects (logit occupancy per covariate unit), a list column, one per covariate in covariate_names order, each NA when not fitted; replicate_variance (squared logit occupancy), between replicates; and residual_variance (squared logit occupancy), run to run within a replicate. Statistics are NA where status is not "fitted". - occupancy_file and runs_file, as absolute paths; trait_name, the runs table's third header; covariate_names; cell_count occupancy rows (cells) read; run_count runs in the runs table; trait_run_count, runs with a trait value (runs); occupancy_runs_not_used; min_runs (runs) and min_replicates (replicates), the thresholds used, yours or mzLib's default; logit_epsilon (fraction, 0 to 1), the clamp used; exclude_ceiling; status_counts, sites (sites) per status; ignored_columns; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: the model and what it leaves out, plus any that apply to this input.

What it is not

It says nothing about whether *detecting* the modification changes with the trait: only quantified cells enter. q adjusts over this call's fitted sites only - not across datasets, and not a target-decoy q-value.

Wraps

Wire verb ptmqtl trait-effects. Generated from the bridge's verb spec ptmqtl.trait-effects.yaml (bridge commit 60b1d25968a1) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • SiteTraitEffects.Fit in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/SiteTraitEffects.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SiteTraitOptions in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/SiteTraitEffects.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SiteTraitEffect in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/SiteTraitEffects.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SiteRunOccupancy in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/SiteOccupancy.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • MixedModel.Fit in mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

occupancy

path; required. The occupancy table ptmqtl occupancy --out writes, one row per (site, run). Columns are found by header name: protein_accession, position (1-based), residue (one letter), modification, run, state (quantified, floor, count_only or not_detected), modified_intensity and covering_intensity (instrument units, finite), unmodified_quantified (true or false), and optionally fraction (fraction, 0 to 1; blank for none), which mzLib then uses instead of modified_intensity / covering_intensity, as it does for a fraction a producer wrote exactly. site_key and category are derived by mzLib and not read; any other column is listed in ignored_columns. A (site, run) given twice is refused, since mzLib's fit would use the first.

runs

path; required. A TSV with a header row, then one row per run: the run (as the occupancy table names it), its biological replicate (the random-intercept group, for example the animal or donor), the trait (its header names the trait; any unit, which effect is then per), then any covariates (each header names one; every value finite for a run with a trait). Columns are by position. A run with a blank, NA or NaN trait is not used, as mzLib reads a run absent from the trait. A run of the occupancy table missing here is not used either, and is listed in occupancy_runs_not_used.

min_runs (wire --min-runs)

int; in runs; default mzLib's SiteTraitOptions.MinRuns, 6 at the pin; range >= 0. The fewest runs contributing a response for a site to be fitted; fewer is below_support. Absent, the bridge sets nothing and mzLib's default applies.

min_replicates (wire --min-replicates)

int; in replicates; default mzLib's SiteTraitOptions.MinReplicates, 4 at the pin; range >= 0. The fewest distinct biological replicates among those runs; fewer is below_support. Absent, mzLib's default applies.

logit_epsilon (wire --logit-epsilon)

float; in fraction (0 to 1); default mzLib's SiteTraitOptions.LogitEpsilon, 5e-5 at the pin (half the 4-decimal resolution of stored fractions); range > 0 and < 0.5. Each fraction is clamped to [epsilon, 1 - epsilon] before the logit, so 0 and 1 have finite logits. Absent, mzLib's default applies.

keep_ceiling (wire --keep-ceiling)

flag; default absent: mzLib's SiteTraitOptions.ExcludeCeiling, true at the pin, so ceilings are left out. Use a run where the site was seen only modified (a fraction of 1 with unmodified_quantified false) as a response, clamped below 1. mzLib leaves such a ceiling out unless asked.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

occupancy_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the occupancy table.

runs_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the runs table.

trait_name

string; never NA. The runs table's third header: the trait.

covariate_names

string[]; never NA. The runs table's headers after the trait, in order; empty without covariates. covariate_effects follows this order.

cell_count

int; in cells; never NA. Occupancy rows read.

run_count

int; in runs; never NA. Runs in the runs table.

trait_run_count

int; in runs; never NA. Runs with a trait value: the runs the design is built over.

occupancy_runs_not_used

string[]; never NA. Runs of the occupancy table with no trait value in the runs table, in ordinal order; their cells were not used.

min_runs

int; in runs; never NA. The support threshold used: as given, or mzLib's default.

min_replicates

int; in replicates; never NA. The replicate threshold used: as given, or mzLib's default.

logit_epsilon

float; in fraction (0 to 1); never NA. The clamp used: as given, or mzLib's default.

exclude_ceiling

bool; never NA. Whether ceiling cells were left out: false with --keep-ceiling, else mzLib's default.

status_counts

map<string,int>; in sites; never NA. Sites per status, keyed by every status value.

ignored_columns

string[]; never NA. Columns of the occupancy file that were not read (other than site_key and category); empty when none.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Sites in the table.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per site with at least one usable response (a quantified cell, not a ceiling unless --keep-ceiling, in a run with a trait), in ordinal site_key order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Six static caveats; plus one listing occupancy runs not used, one counting sites not fitted by status, and one naming columns not read, when they apply.

Columns of records

site_key

string; never NA. mzLib's ModificationSite.Key, as ptmqtl occupancy writes it.

protein_accession

string; never NA. The site's protein.

position

int; never NA. 1-based residue position, as ptmqtl occupancy.

residue

string; never NA. The one-letter residue.

modification

string; never NA. Category:IdWithMotif.

status

string; never NA. fitted | below_support (fewer runs or replicates than min_runs or min_replicates) | too_few_observations | rank_deficient | too_few_groups | variance_ratio_at_limit | not_converged (mzLib's MixedModel could not fit it, as stats fit names those outcomes). Only fitted rows carry statistics.

effect

float; in logit occupancy per trait unit; NA when not fitted (see status). The change in logit(occupancy) per unit of the trait, other covariates held fixed. exp(effect) is the odds ratio of the modified form per trait unit.

standard_error

float; in logit occupancy per trait unit; NA when not fitted. Standard error of effect.

df

float; in degrees of freedom; NA when not fitted. Denominator degrees of freedom of the t test, by nlme's containment rule: for a trait constant within each replicate, replicates - 1 - the between-replicate coefficients.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted. Two-sided p-value of the trait coefficient.

q

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted, so not in the family. Benjamini-Hochberg over the sites with a p-value in this call. Not a target-decoy q-value.

runs

int; in runs; never NA. Runs contributing a response.

replicates

int; in replicates; never NA. Distinct biological replicates among those runs.

median_fraction

float; in fraction (0 to 1); never NA. Median occupancy over the contributing runs, before the clamp.

covariate_effects

float[]; in logit occupancy per covariate unit; never NA. One coefficient per covariate, in covariate_names order; each element null when the site was not fitted. Empty without covariates.

replicate_variance

float; in squared logit occupancy; NA when not fitted. Between-replicate variance of logit occupancy (the random intercept).

residual_variance

float; in squared logit occupancy; NA when not fitted. Within-replicate (run-to-run) variance of logit occupancy.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

occupancy or runs missing, blank or not found; min-runs or min-replicates not an integer or below 0; logit-epsilon not a number, or not above 0 and below 0.5; an option given without a value; keep-ceiling written with a value

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the occupancy file empty, header-only, missing a column, with a repeated column name, a row of the wrong width, a position that is not an integer, a residue that is not one letter, a state that is not one of the four, an intensity that is not finite, a fraction that is not a number, unmodified_quantified not true or false, an empty accession, modification or run, or a (site, run) twice

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the runs file with fewer than three columns, a repeated header after the replicate, a row of the wrong width, an empty or repeated run, or a trait or covariate that is not a number

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input, in its own words: a run with a trait and no replicate; a run with a trait whose covariates are not all finite; a design (intercept, trait, covariates over the runs with a trait) not of full column rank, such as a constant trait

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Per site, logit(occupancy) = b0 + b_trait trait + the covariates + a random intercept per biological replicate + error, fitted by REML (mzLib's MixedModel). Repeated runs of one replicate (technical injections) are not counted as independent: a trait constant within each replicate is tested at the between-replicate degrees of freedom.

  • Only quantified cells are responses; floor, count_only and not_detected cells are left out, never entered as 0. This is the intensity part of the question: it says nothing about whether detecting the modification changes with the trait.

  • Ceiling cells are left out unless keep-ceiling.

  • Fractions are clamped to [logit_epsilon, 1 - logit_epsilon] before the logit. effect is per unit of the trait as given: rescale the trait to change the unit.

  • A site with fewer than min_runs runs or min_replicates replicates is below_support, with null statistics; a site with no usable response does not appear.

  • q adjusts over this call's fitted sites only: not across datasets, and not a target-decoy q-value.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.ptmqtl.trait_effects

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::ptmqtl::trait_effects_with with TraitEffectsOptions

  • R (mzLibR): ptmqtl_trait_effects

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

References

  • doi:10.2307/2529876: the random-intercept linear mixed model fitted per site (Laird and Ware, Biometrics 38:963, 1982)

  • doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x: the step-up adjustment behind q (Benjamini and Hochberg, J R Stat Soc B 57:289, 1995)

See also

ptmqtl_occupancy, stats_fit_mixed for the same model on any responses

Examples


# mzLib's TraitDesign: six replicates at three doses, two injections each, with
# logit(occupancy) = -2 + 0.5 x dose + a replicate offset. trait_runs.tsv gives each run's
# replicate, dose and an injection covariate; trait_occupancy.tsv is ptmqtl_occupancy(out = )'s.
data <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", package = "mzLibR")
fit <- ptmqtl_trait_effects(file.path(data, "trait_occupancy.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "trait_runs.tsv"))
fit
#> <mzlibr_trait_effects> 2 sites against dose, given injection (min 6 runs, 4 replicates)
#>   fitted 2, below_support 0, too_few_observations 0, rank_deficient 0, too_few_groups 0, variance_ratio_at_limit 0, not_converged 0
fit$records[, c("protein_accession", "status", "effect", "df", "runs", "replicates")]
#>   protein_accession status    effect df runs replicates
#> 1     CENSORED_SITE fitted 0.5428795  3   10          5
#> 2        TRAIT_SITE fitted 0.5008514  4   12          6
